source_policy: Family appearance and roofline alignment are user observations; floor counts are from SFU official housing/building records. Retain per-building door locations, foundations, rotations, actual geometry and terrain. Roof alignment must be verified using terrain and photos; do not force a roof height by moving/floating foundations or silently swapping confirmed storey counts.

family_definitions.shared: one photo-matched exterior architecture model, identical characteristic exterior modules, window rhythm, color/material family and roofline treatment when supported by photos
family_definitions.unique: building stable ID, actual XZ, rotation, East 7/West 8 storeys per SFU, foundation/grade, entrance position/signage, podium geometry or verified exceptions

roof_alignment.user_report: East and West rooflines appear aligned in world elevation although ground levels differ
roof_alignment.target: align absolute visible roofline Y if site evidence supports it; no arbitrary building stretching
roof_alignment.grade_direction_caveat: User says West is on higher ground and one floor shorter, but official SFU counts West as one floor taller. For equal storey heights and coincident roofs, East foundation would be higher than West. Do not assume either grade direction until surveyed terrain is checked.

family_definitions.shared: one architectural master for Barbara Rae, Pauline Jewett and Shadbolt; all three use this combined photo family folder, and per-building variants only with direct evidence
family_definitions.unique: actual stable ID, XZ/rotation, site grade, entry positions, signage, any observed instance-specific facade exceptions

family_definitions.shared: repeatable townhouse building shell/windows/materials/roof details when photo-verified
family_definitions.unique: actual block dimensions, varying configuration if observed, transform/rotation, grade, access door side and circulation

do_not_assume: An identical-looking tower has an identical entrance orientation
East and West have the same number of floors
North Towers are copies of modern East/West towers
Every townhouse building has an identical slope, orientation or dimensions
A photo of one building proves colors of another without checking
Old Google aerial imagery depicts the new modern towers
The user-reported West-higher/one-floor-fewer arrangement overrides documented East seven and West eight storeys
Roofline alignment can be simulated by changing tower floor counts, arbitrary Y offsets, or distorting floor heights
All North Towers need separate modeling passes or separate photo directories
